chunks: "Indeed, when Dhu al-Qarnayn reached the barrier, he passed beyond it and entered into the darkness. Then suddenly he came upon an angel standing upon a mountain whose height was five hundred cubits. The angel said to him, 'O Dhu al-Qarnayn, was there not a path behind you?' Dhu al-Qarnayn said to him, 'Who are you?' He said, 'I am an angel from among the angels of the Most Merciful, entrusted with this mountain. There is no mountain that Allah has created except that it has a vein connected to this mountain. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills to cause a city to quake, He reveals to me, and I make it quake.'"

key_terms.الرَّحْمَنِ: the Most Merciful, referring to Allah
key_terms.السَّدِّ: the barrier or wall reached by Dhu al-Qarnayn
key_terms.الظُّلُمَاتِ: the darknesses into which he entered
key_terms.ذَا الْقَرْنَيْنِ: Dhu al-Qarnayn, the figure described in the narrative
key_terms.عِرْقٌ: a connecting root or vein linking mountains
key_terms.مَدِينَةً: a city affected by an earthquake
key_terms.مَلَكٍ: an angel encountered in the account
key_terms.يُزَلْزِلَ: to cause to quake or shake

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the cause of earthquakes in the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts an encounter of Dhu al-Qarnayn beyond the barrier, where he meets an angel charged with a great mountain connected to all other mountains. The report presents earthquakes as occurring by the command of Allah عزّ وجلّ through an appointed angel, reflecting divine control over cosmic events.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1511 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"When Dhu al-Qarnayn reached the barrier (the wall), he passed beyond it and entered the darkness. There, he encountered an angel standing upon a mountain whose height was five hundred cubits.
The angel said to him, 'O’ Dhu al-Qarnayn, was there no way back behind you?'
Dhu al-Qarnayn asked: 'Who are you?'
The angel replied: 'I am an angel from among the angels of the Most Merciful, assigned to this mountain. There is no mountain that Allah (swt) has created except that it has a root connected to this mountain. When Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, intends to cause an earthquake in a city, He commands me, and I cause it to quake.'"
